name: bad-frag-sibling-altered
summary: Full-bleed hero running shader.gallery's gloam: four twilight poles drifting through near-black while one blooms off-centre like the last light in the sky, with a matched CSS dusk as the resting state.

colors.description: Four poles; index 1 is the luminous one that blooms. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette.

driftSpeed.description: How fast the twilight poles drift; 0 holds the dusk almost still. Upstream default, range 0 to 0.7.

glow.description: Brightness of the luminous pole blooming through the dark; 0 leaves an even twilight. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.4.

warp.description: Organic distortion of the colour edges; low is smooth, high adds folds. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.5.

deviations.what: The four u_palette colours are ours, not upstream's `nocturne` preset.
deviations.why: gloam/meta.json names a palette as a string only; the table it resolves against lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor. Ours is a dark-site nocturne chosen to match the CSS resting state, which reads the same --fx-c1..--fx-c4.

deviations.what: No post chain: upstream's poster runs duotone, grain 0.055 and vignette 0.40 over the shader output.
deviations.why: The post chain is also in @shader-gallery/runtime. Our output is the raw shader, so it will not match the upstream poster. The section's own CSS grain layer covers the banding the poster's grain was there for.

deviations.what: Rendered through paw-fx's own WebGL runtime (effects/_shared/glsl-mount.js) rather than @shader-gallery/runtime.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream ships the .frag with no module around it. The GLSL itself is byte-identical to upstream and lives in shader.frag beside index.js.
